what_happened.line: The committee voted to authorize the manager to buy lighting equipment from JML, within a not-to-exceed cap, after comparing three vendor quotes.
A motion to buy the Datavideo HS-1300 switcher for no more than a set cap was amended, and the amended motion to research further before buying passed.
The manager will gather prices, a third quote, loaner options and a Mass Access forum answer on the switcher and bring them to the next meeting.
The manager raised that the production technician budget for a 20-hour week does not match the hourly rates of the approved pay grade.
Video on demand and closed captioning through Castis stay on the next agenda as separate items, with ARPA seen as a poor fit for an ongoing annual fee.

why_it_matters: The committee spends cable access money on studio equipment, and the lighting purchase and the deferred switcher show how it chooses vendors and caps what it pays.
Video on demand and captioning carry annual fees, so they would be continuing costs for the committee's operating budget, which a member said goes mostly to salaries, rather than one-time purchases.
The technician pay mismatch and the studio space question could both change what the committee asks to spend in future budgets.
watch_next: The next meeting, tentatively April 4 at 7 p.m. and to be settled by email, where the switcher research and the captioning and video on demand costs are due back.
Whether the technician pay mismatch goes back to personnel, which the minutes leave undecided.
